approval.cost: No price or cost amount was stated on the pages read
approval.trigger: App Review is required for Advanced Access: 'If this new app needs Advanced Access, App Review is required.' The access levels are the cap structure: 'Standard Access if your app serves Instagram professional accounts you own or manage and have added to your app in the App Dashboard'; 'Advanced Access if your app serves Instagram professional accounts you don't own or manage'. In other words, serving other people's accounts is exactly what triggers review; your own or managed accounts can be added in the App Dashboard under Standard Access. Advanced Access goes through Meta's App Review (see the Facebook guide for the shared process: app verification plus permissions review, business verification for advanced access); no Instagram-specific review timeline or fee is stated on the pages read.
approval.wait: Not stated (see the Facebook guide: Meta states no App Review duration on the readable pages)

blockers.detail: The Instagram Login product requires a Business-type Meta app. 'App type must be Business; if not, create a new app and select Business.' An app created with another type cannot simply switch.
blockers.howToClear: Create the Meta app as type Business from the start.
blockers.title: App type must be Business

blockers.detail: Refresh requires the token be 'at least 24 hours old and valid' and instagram_business_basic granted, and 'Tokens that have not been refreshed in 60 days will expire'. A connection left untouched for 60 days is dead even though nothing was revoked.
blockers.howToClear: Refresh long-lived tokens on a schedule well inside 60 days.
blockers.title: Refresh window rules

blockers.detail: The Instagram API with Instagram Login 'cannot access ads or tagging'. If the product needs ads data or hashtag search, that lives on the Facebook Login variant (accounts linked to a Facebook Page), a different setup with its own review surface.
blockers.howToClear: Choose the variant by required capability before building: Instagram Login for publishing/comments/messages/insights/mentions; Facebook Login variant for hashtag search and Page-linked accounts.
blockers.title: Capability ceiling of the Instagram Login variant

flavor.recommended: A Business-type Meta app with the Instagram product, using the Instagram API with Instagram Login (Business Login OAuth flow)
flavor.why: The Instagram API with Instagram Login manages Instagram Business/Creator (professional) accounts WITHOUT requiring a Facebook Page, and supports comment moderation, content publishing, Media Insights, Mentions, and Messaging; a stated limitation is that it 'cannot access ads or tagging'. Setup: the app type must be Business; add the Instagram product and configure Business login settings in the App Dashboard (Instagram > API setup with Instagram login), copy the Embed URL into a link/button. The account object is the IG User (user_id <IG_ID>, an app-scoped id, username, name, account_type Business or Media_Creator, profile_picture_url, followers_count, follows_count, media_count), reached via GET graph.instagram.com/v26.0/me and /<IG_ID>/media. Scopes use the new names: instagram_business_basic, instagram_business_content_publish, instagram_business_manage_messages, instagram_business_manage_comments (the old business_* names were deprecated January 27, 2025).

humanMust: Create a Meta app of type Business (an existing non-Business app cannot be converted)
Add the Instagram product and configure Business login settings in the App Dashboard; copy the Embed URL into your product
For Advanced Access: submit for Meta App Review (see the Facebook guide)
name: Instagram
nuances: Token endpoints live on two hosts: the code exchange is at api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token, while the long-lived exchange and refresh are at graph.instagram.com (access_token?grant_type=ig_exchange_token and refresh_access_token?grant_type=ig_refresh_token), and API calls go to graph.instagram.com/v26.0.
The authorize URL accepts optional enable_fb_login and force_reauth parameters alongside client_id (the Instagram App ID), redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, and state.

App Dashboard-generated tokens are long-lived (60 days), unlike flow-issued short-lived tokens (1 hour), which matters for testing: a dashboard token behaves differently from a real user's first token.
prerequisites: A Meta app of type Business
An Instagram professional (Business/Creator) account to connect
For other people's accounts: Advanced Access via App Review

steps.detail: Create a Meta app and select type Business. Add the Instagram product; in Instagram > API setup with Instagram login, configure Business login settings and note the Instagram App ID; copy the Embed URL into a link or button in your product.
steps.title: Create a Business app; add the Instagram product

steps.detail: Authorize at instagram.com/oauth/authorize (client_id = Instagram App ID, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, optional state, enable_fb_login, force_reauth). POST the returned code to api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token (with client_secret and grant_type=authorization_code) for a short-lived token (valid 1 hour), the Instagram-scoped user ID, and granted permissions. The code is 'valid for 1 hour and can only be used once'.
steps.title: Authorize; exchange the code (1-hour token)

steps.detail: GET graph.instagram.com/access_token?grant_type=ig_exchange_token (server-side) for a long-lived token (valid 60 days). Refresh at graph.instagram.com/refresh_access_token?grant_type=ig_refresh_token for 'another 60 days'. Call the API at graph.instagram.com/v26.0 (/me, /<IG_ID>/media).
steps.title: Exchange for long-lived; refresh; call the API

steps.detail: If the app serves accounts you don't own or manage, request Advanced Access through Meta App Review before onboarding those users. Standard Access covers accounts you own or manage and have added in the App Dashboard.
steps.title: (Advanced Access) Submit for App Review

tagline: Instagram professional accounts without a Facebook Page, through a Business-type Meta app: one-hour tokens exchanged into 60-day tokens, and App Review the moment you serve accounts you do not own or manage.
